question: What is the primary focus of rehabilitation compared to acute medical care?

options.B: Surgical intervention to cure the underlying disease
options.C: Providing palliative comfort during terminal illness
options.D: Complete eradication of chronic pathological processes

explanation: Rehabilitation focuses on helping patients adapt to altered abilities and achieve maximum independence rather than curing the acute disease process. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h1)

question: A patient views themselves as helpless after a stroke. How should the nurse apply rehabilitation philosophy?

options.A: Take over all daily activities to prevent patient frustration
options.B: Focus strictly on administering prescribed medications on time
options.C: Encourage the patient to actively participate in self-care tasks
options.D: Wait until physical strength fully returns before starting tasks

explanation: The rehabilitation philosophy emphasizes patient partnership and maximizing remaining strengths through active participation. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h1)

question: Which professional specializes in helping patients regain fine motor skills for daily activities?
explanation: Occupational therapists focus on fine motor coordination and activities of daily living such as eating, bathing, and dressing. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h2)

question: A stroke patient struggles to swallow food safely during meals. Which team member should the nurse consult first?
explanation: Speech-language pathologists are experts in assessing and managing swallowing disorders and communication impairments. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h2)

question: At what point does the rehabilitation process ideally begin for an injured patient?

options.A: After chronic complications have fully developed
options.B: When the patient requests physical therapy
options.D: Only after complete discharge from the hospital

explanation: Rehabilitation nursing assessment and preventative positioning start right away during the acute phase of care. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h3)

question: What characterizes the supportive or maintenance phase of rehabilitation?

options.A: Immediate surgical intervention for acute traumatic injury
options.B: Intensive daily therapy to recover lost physical movements
options.C: Rapid transition to independent unassisted community living
options.D: Sustaining achieved functional levels and preventing regression

explanation: The supportive phase focuses on preserving functional gains over the long term, especially in chronic or progressive illnesses. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h3)

question: What is the primary focus of a rehabilitation nursing assessment?

options.A: Functional capacity and daily living abilities
options.B: Identification of the primary disease pathogen
options.D: Surgical history and past medication allergies

explanation: Rehabilitation nursing prioritizes evaluating how a condition impacts the patient's functional independence and daily activities. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h4)

question: Why must rehabilitation goals be developed in direct collaboration with the patient?

options.A: To ensure the family takes full financial responsibility for equipment
options.B: To relieve the nursing staff from designing the care plan independently
options.C: To ensure the objectives are personally meaningful and motivate compliance
options.D: To satisfy hospital accreditation requirements for clinical documentation

explanation: Patient participation in goal setting aligns therapy with personal values, significantly boosting motivation and active engagement. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h4)

question: A patient with hemiplegia struggles to button a shirt during morning care. How should the nurse intervene?

options.A: Encourage the patient to use adaptive buttoning aids and try independently
options.B: Leave the patient undressed until the occupational therapist arrives
options.C: Insist that family members visit every morning to dress the patient
options.D: Complete the dressing quickly to save time for morning medication rounds

explanation: The nurse should promote independence by providing adaptive equipment and allowing time for the patient to practice self-care skills. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of integrating rehabilitation principles into routine daily care?

options.A: To reinforce therapy practices continuously throughout the day
options.B: To decrease the need for specialized nursing documentation
options.C: To shorten the overall duration of hospital admission
options.D: To reduce the workload of specialized physical therapists

explanation: Consistent reinforcement during daily routines helps patients habituate new skills and transfer them to real-life situations. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h5)

question: Which nursing intervention helps prevent deep vein thrombosis in an immobile patient?

options.A: Restricting fluid intake to decrease systemic blood pressure
options.B: Placing the patient in a prone position for the entire day
options.C: Applying compression stockings and encouraging hydration
options.D: Avoiding all passive range-of-motion exercises to rest limbs

explanation: Compression stockings and adequate hydration improve venous return and reduce the formation of blood clots in immobile patients. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h6)

question: Why are passive range-of-motion exercises regularly performed on paralyzed limbs?

options.A: To reverse permanent nerve damage in the affected limbs
options.B: To prevent joint contractures and maintain muscle flexibility
options.C: To stimulate rapid bone marrow production of red blood cells
options.D: To increase systemic blood pressure in hypotensive patients

explanation: Passive range-of-motion exercises keep joints mobile and prevent permanent shortening of muscles and tendons known as contractures. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h6)

question: When should the discharge planning process ideally begin for a rehabilitation patient?

options.A: After the final multidisciplinary team meeting
options.B: On the day of admission to the facility
options.C: Twenty-four hours prior to hospital discharge
options.D: When the family requests permission to take the patient home

explanation: Early discharge planning ensures adequate time to arrange home modifications, equipment, and caregiver training before the patient leaves. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h7)

question: An elderly patient with a wheelchair is preparing to go home. What is an important nursing action before discharge?

options.A: Instructing the family to purchase a completely new house
options.B: Ensuring home doorways and bathrooms can accommodate the wheelchair
options.C: Discontinuing all physical therapy exercises upon leaving the hospital
options.D: Recommending long-term institutional placement instead of home care

explanation: Checking the home environment for accessibility prevents safety hazards and promotes successful community reintegration. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h7)
